raw_history.content:
A Spring Boot application is producing incorrect behavior.

FAILING ENDPOINT
  GET /bug/reflection-v2?type=DELIVERY&payload=alice@example.com

EXPECTED
  Delivery confirmation sent to alice@example.com
  Server log contains: [DELIVERY] Sending confirmation to: alice@example.com

OBSERVED
  HTTP 200 returned. No delivery occurs.
  Server log contains: [AUDIT] Recorded event payload: alice@example.com

No exception. No stack trace. The endpoint returns "ok".

Investigate the root cause. The application source is in:
  src/main/java/com/example/demo/
  src/main/resources/

Found it. The bug is on line 11 of `application.properties`:

```
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler
```

The `delivery` key is mapped to `AuditHandler` instead of `DeliveryHandler`. That's why the log shows `[AUDIT] Recorded event payload:` instead of `[DELIVERY] Sending confirmation to:` — the wrong handler class is wired up in config.

Thought: The causality data is confirmed by reading the source. `application.properties` line 11 maps `notification.handlers.delivery` to `AuditHandler` instead of `DeliveryHandler`. At runtime, when `DELIVERY` is dispatched, `NotificationService2` looks up the registry, finds `AuditHandler` (because that's what the config binds), instantiates it reflectively, and calls `handle()` — producing the `[AUDIT]` log instead of `[DELIVERY]`. The `alert` key has `DeliveryHandler`, which is also wrong (they appear swapped).
